exposure: Mode of delivery (vaginal delivery vs. elective cesarean section)
cohort: 53 healthy women with a singleton pregnancy and more than 36 completed weeks of gestation
finding: Vaginal delivery was associated with significantly higher concentrations of AVP and copeptin, but not OT, in infants' arterial umbilical cord blood compared to elective cesarean section.
mod_finding: Infants born vaginally had significantly higher levels of arginine vasopressin and copeptin, indicating higher birth stress, compared to infants born via elective cesarean section.
